_comment: Copy to config/vdclient.json and edit. Every value here is the default,
so an empty object {} behaves identically. Keys starting with _ or $ are
ignored. Environment overrides use VDCLIENT_<SECTION>_<KEY>, e.g.

identity._comment: What the Quest sees in its computer list.
identity.name: Linux Test PC
identity._streamer_version: Version-gated by the app; must be close enough to the installed streamer to pass its update checks.
identity._os_name: Must be 'Windows' or 'MacOS'. Anything else makes the Quest's deserializer throw and silently drop this computer from the list.
identity._adapters: Advertised in PrivateAdapters. The Quest derives our real address from the UDP reply's source, so this is mostly cosmetic.

video._size: null = detect the primary output and align down to a multiple of 16. An explicit value must already be a multiple of 16, or the encoder pads and signals a crop the Quest's decoder may ignore, leaving a black bar along one edge.
video._encoder: 'h264_vaapi' (Intel iGPU) or 'libx264' (software). VAAPI falls back to software automatically if no render node is found or the encode probe fails.
video._source: 'auto', 'test' (pattern), 'x11', 'kmsgrab', 'kms'. 'auto' picks x11 when an X server is running, then upgrades a single full-screen monitor to zero-copy kmsgrab when ffmpeg has CAP_SYS_ADMIN.
_monitors: One entry per monitor, at most 3 (the Quest configures 3 decoders).
[x, y, w, h]          -> a capture region of the primary screen
[null, {"virtual": true}]         real screen + one virtual monitor
All monitors encode at the same width/height; per-monitor bounds only

tunables._comment: Timings and buffer sizes. Change only with a reason.
